history.summary: Old, well-known Kali temple on Kadani Road in the Tinplate area of Golmuri, Jamshedpur - the neighbourhood developed around the Tinplate Company of India (production began 1923), and the temple is a landmark of that company-town area. Founding date and history are UNVERIFIED in web sources; reviews describe it as one of the oldest and most revered Maa Kali temples in Jamshedpur. The complex holds shrines to Goddess Kali, Lord Shiva and Shani Dev, with two halls for functions and puja-material shops in front. It draws large crowds on Saturdays and Tuesdays (weekly Saturday evening aarti is popular). CSV town 'Jamshedpur' is coarse - corrected to Golmuri (Tinplate), Jamshedpur.

name: Tinplate Kali Mandir
town_description: Jamshedpur, known as the Steel City of India, is the largest city in Jharkhand. Founded by Jamsetji Tata as a planned industrial town around Tata Steel (TISCO), the settlement was called Sakchi until it was renamed Jamshedpur in 1919. The city sits at the confluence of the Kharkai and Subarnarekha rivers in East Singhbhum district, and its neighbourhoods (Telco, Golmuri, Sakchi, Kadma, Parsudih, Sidhgora) grew around Tata Steel and its subsidiary companies. Golmuri was developed as the company town of the Tinplate Company of India.

travel.road: On Kadani Road, Tinplate area, Golmuri - on the main road, easily reached by auto and city bus

visitor_information.best_time: October to February (winter); Kali Puja (Diwali) is the major festival
visitor_information.opening_hours: Hours not published by any reliable source (verify); Saturdays and Tuesdays see heavy crowds, especially the Saturday evening aarti
